facts.raw_span: 87-year-old Cantonese-speaking man
Alzheimer’s dementia, hypertension, stroke, hyperlipidaemia, gout, peptic ulcer, and chronic kidney disease
one week of increasing left leg pain and weakness
impaired mobility
a single episode of urinary incontinence
anorexia and a 12% body-weight loss over six months
blood pressure was 88/45 mmHg
heart rate 96/min
elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 76 mg/L, WCC 11.9 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.5 × 10^9/L)
pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury
bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy
no evidence of trochanteric bursitis

concepts.why: The patient presented with increasing left leg pain and weakness, and the MRI showed bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy.
The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease, and the laboratory results demonstrated pre-renal acute-on-chronic kidney injury.
The patient presented with elevated inflammatory markers and a low blood pressure, which are consistent with sepsis.
The patient has a history of gout, and the presentation of increasing left leg pain and weakness could be consistent with a gouty flare.
The patient presented with impaired mobility and a significant weight loss, which are consistent with deconditioning syndrome.
The patient presented with a low blood pressure, which is consistent with hypotension.
The patient presented with increasing left leg pain and weakness, and the MRI showed bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement.
The patient presented with a single episode of urinary incontinence, which could be consistent with a neurological or geriatric condition.
It explains the uncovered finding of low blood pressure at 88/45 mmHg.

rationales.F11: Bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and left-sided insertional tendinopathy are consistent with ilipsoas tendinitis.
